Article.ArticleTitle: Mechanism investigation of Platycodon grandiflorum active Ingredients in regulating epithelial-mesenchymal transition and airway remodeling in asthma via modulation of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis and IL-17A/MAPK pathway.

Abstract.AbstractText: Platycodon grandiflorum (Jacq.) A.DC. is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb recognized for its dual role as both food and medicine, renowned for its effects of diffusing the lung, alleviating sore throat, promoting expectoration, and facilitating pus drainage. In traditional medicinal practice, it is often used in combination with herbs such as Ephedra sinica, Prunus armeniaca and Glycyrrhiza uralensis utilized to mitigate symptoms associated with asthma, bronchitis, and other respiratory diseases. However, the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of its principal bioactive components in treating asthma remain insufficiently characterized.

To investigate the pharmacological effects and elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which triterpenoid saponins derived from Platycodon grandiflorum (PL-TS) inhibit airway epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and attenuate airway remodeling in asthma.

Initially, the chemical constituents of the triterpenoid saponin fraction extracted from Platycodon grandiflorum (Jacq.) A. DC. (PL-TS) were identified by Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography Tandem Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-MS). Subsequently, network pharmacology approaches were employed to predict potential therapeutic targets and core signaling pathways of PL-TS in asthma. An OVA-induced asthmatic mouse model was established for in vivo experiments. Airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) was assessed via whole-body plethysmography (WBP), and histopathological changes in lung tissues were examined via hematoxylin-eosin (HE), Masson's trichrome, and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining. Human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) were utilized to establish an IL-17A-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) model in vitro. Finally, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), immunohistochemistry (IHC), quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and Western blotting (WB) were employed to investigate the modulatory effects of PL-TS on proteins associated with airway remodeling, the IL-17A/MAPK signaling pathway, and the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis in both asthmatic mice and cellular models.

UPLC-MS/MS analysis identified 38 triterpenoid saponins from PL-TS, providing a chemical foundation for subsequent mechanistic studies. Network pharmacology analysis revealed that the principal targets of PL-TS were predominantly enriched within the IL-17A signaling pathway. In OVA-induced asthmatic mice, PL-TS significantly attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, mucus hypersecretion, and collagen deposition in lung tissues, while markedly reducing serum levels of IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, and OVA-IgE in vivo. Furthermore, PL-TS was found to inhibit the activation of the IL-17A/MAPK and Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A signaling pathways in both mouse lung tissue and stimulated cells, while downregulating EMT-related protein Vimentin, Snail, and N-cadherin, upregulating expression of E-cadherin. suppressing the phosphorylation of p38, ERK, and JNK in the MAPK pathway. In addition, PL-TS downregulated Sirt6 expression and reduced RORγt and IL-17A levels, suggesting a potential involvement of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A regulatory axis, although the precise epigenetic mechanism requires further investigation.

This study demonstrated that the PL-TS significantly alleviated airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and airway remodeling in asthma model. The effects were associated with suppression of the IL-17A/MAPK pathway and downregulation of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis, suggesting a potential dual mechanism that highlight its therapeutic potential.

Article.ArticleTitle: SPECTRE-guided discovery of polyacetylenes from Codonopsis pilosula with neuroprotective activity against OGD/R-induced injury.

Abstract.AbstractText: SPECTRE-guided interpretation of HSQC data was employed to prioritize polyacetylene-enriched fractions during the phytochemical investigation of Codonopsis pilosula, providing an efficient strategy for targeted discovery of structurally diverse natural products. Guided isolation yielded 20 polyacetylenes, including nine previously undescribed compounds (1-9). Their structures and stereochemical features were elucidated through integrated spectroscopic analysis, DP4+ calculations, ECD simulation, and Mo₂(OAc)₄-induced CD experiments. In the HT22 oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation model, compound 7 exhibited the strongest neuroprotective activity among the isolated polyacetylenes, with an EC₅₀ of 4.51 ± 1.26 μM, representing the first systematic evaluation of the neuroprotective potential of polyacetylene constituents from C. pilosula. To investigate the possible involvement of CYP1B1, computational docking and molecular dynamics analyses were combined with CETSA and Western blot experiments. The combined results supported CYP1B1 as a candidate protein associated with compound 7.

Article.ArticleTitle: A novel deep learning-based peak detection technique for in vivo metabolite analysis of triterpenoids from Eleutherococcus senticosus leaves in Parkinson's disease mice.

Abstract.AbstractText: To address the challenges in mass spectrometry data processing, including poor detection of low-abundance metabolites, severe noise interference, and the reliance on labor-intensive parameter tuning in conventional peak detection methods, a deep learning-based peak detection algorithm termed MSPeakNet was developed. The model used a multi-scale convolutional module and a U-net encoder-decoder architecture integrated with an attention mechanism, enabling high-precision peak identification and noise reduction in complex biological matrices. MSPeakNet achieved precision and F1 scores comparable to CWT, with superior noise robustness, while maintaining competitive recall. The developed method was subsequently applied to the in vivo metabolite profiling of total triterpenoids from Eleutherococcus senticosus leaves (ESLT) in an MPTP-induced mouse model of Parkinson's disease (PD) using UPLC-Q-TOF/MS analysis. A total of 143 ESLT-related compounds, comprising 88 prototypes and 55 metabolites, were identified in plasma, urine, feces, and brain tissue, of which 16 prototypes were detected in brain tissue. Pharmacodynamic evaluation further confirmed that ESLT significantly ameliorated MPTP-induced motor dysfunction and dopaminergic neuronal loss. Comparative analysis further revealed distinct profiles of ESLT-related differential compounds between PD model and normal mice across multiple biological matrices; 14, 9, 6, and 4 differential metabolites were identified in feces, urine, plasma, and brain, respectively, suggesting that disease status may affect the biotransformation, distribution, and elimination of ESLT constituents. A robust and efficient deep learning-based approach for mass spectrometry peak detection was thereby established, and critical experimental evidence was provided for the discovery of anti-Parkinsonian active ingredients and quality markers from E. senticosus leaves.

Article.ArticleTitle: Associations of grip strength, muscle mass, and fat-to-muscle ratio with advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in chinese community adults.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a global health challenge. However, few studies have explored the associations between muscle health and CKM syndrome. This study aimed to investigate the associations between appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM), grip strength, and fat-to-muscle ratio (FMR) and advanced CKM syndrome in a Chinese community-based population.

We conducted an observational study involving 7,330 Chinese adults. CKM syndrome is categorized into five stages, with stages 3-4 defined as advanced CKM syndrome. An electronic dynamometer and bioelectrical impedance analysis were used to measure grip strength, ASM, and FMR. The FMR was calculated as fat mass divided by muscle mass, and ASM/BMI as ASM divided by body mass index (BMI). Associations of grip strength, ASM/BMI, and FMR with advanced CKM syndrome were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, with subgroup analyses by age and sex. Subgroup analyses were further conducted to explore potential interactions.

Advanced CKM syndrome was identified in 8.57% of participants. Higher ASM/BMI (Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.15-0.45) and grip strength (Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.30-0.59) were inversely linked to the likelihood of having advanced CKM syndrome (P-trend < 0.001). Conversely, a higher FMR was associated with higher odds of advanced CKM syndrome (Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.26-3.89; P-trend < 0.05). Furthermore, subgroup analyses showed that the inverse association between grip strength and advanced CKM syndrome was stronger among females (P for interaction = 0.007). A nonlinear, L-shaped association was observed between grip strength and advanced CKM syndrome, with an inflection point at 26.2 kg in females.

Lower ASM/BMI and grip strength, and a higher FMR are associated with an increased likelihood of advanced CKM syndrome. Additionally, a plausible grip-strength threshold (~ 26.2 kg) was identified among females. These findings support evaluating muscle health for risk stratification in CKM syndrome.

Article.ArticleTitle: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Analysis of the UK Biobank.

Abstract.AbstractText: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its associations across cardiovascular and microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes remain incompletely characterized.

We retrospectively analyzed 17 893 UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes, whole-exome sequencing, and no prevalent cardiovascular or microvascular complications. CHIP was defined from the curated UK Biobank call set by ≥1 driver variant with a variant allele fraction ≥2%. Associations with incident outcomes were evaluated using Fine-Gray models with multiple imputation for missing covariates. Driver-gene, clone-size, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were exploratory.

CHIP was present in 670 participants (3.7%) over a median follow-up of 14.6 years. CHIP was associated with the composite cardiovascular outcome (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.19 [95% CI, 1.00-1.42]), with heart failure showing the clearest component association (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.13-1.81]); acute coronary syndrome and stroke were not significantly associated. CHIP was also associated with the composite microvascular outcome (SHR, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.15-1.56]), broad chronic kidney disease (SHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.05-1.57]), and retinopathy (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.15-1.77]) but not neuropathy or strict diabetes-specific nephropathy. Ten-year adjusted risk differences were 1.94% and 3.46% for the cardiovascular and microvascular composites, respectively. Among 2919 proteins, ZBP1 (Z-DNA-binding protein 1) was the only protein retained after false-discovery-rate correction; no metabolite module was associated with CHIP after correction, whereas selected lipoprotein and amino acid/lactate modules were associated with cardiovascular outcomes, particularly heart failure.

In adults with type 2 diabetes, CHIP was associated with a higher risk of incident microvascular complications and, among cardiovascular outcomes, most consistently with heart failure. Exploratory multiomic findings, including a protein-wide ZBP1 signal and selected metabolic associations with cardiovascular outcomes, provided additional biological context but require independent validation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Targeting NIK-mediated microglial polarization: a novel therapeutic strategy for diabetic retinopathy.

Abstract.AbstractText: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a sight-threatening microvascular complication characterized by blood-retina barrier (BRB) disruption. While inflammation is central to early DR, the role of the non-canonical NF-κB pathway remains poorly understood.

We established a murine DR model and performed RNA-seq. Retinal microglial activation and the expression of NF-κB-inducing kinase (NIK) were assessed via immunohistochemistry and Western blot. In vitro, we employed AGEs-treated HMC3 microglia and a co-culture system with human retinal microvascular endothelial cells (hRMECs) under NIK knockdown or pharmacological inhibition (using the NIK inhibitor B022). Molecular mechanisms were delineated using ChIP-qPCR and pathway analysis.

RNA-seq revealed significant enrichment of non-canonical NF-κB signaling in DR. NIK was significantly upregulated in DR retinas, specifically in microglia. NIK knockdown in vitro attenuated microglial activation, suppressed pro-inflammatory M1 markers (iNOS, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), and promoted anti-inflammatory M2 markers (Arg-1, IL-10). Mechanistically, NIK drives microglial polarization via the non-canonical NF-κB pathway (IKKα/p52). In co-culture, NIK knockdown or B022 treatment rescued hRMECs from AGEs-activated microglia-induced dysfunction, improving viability, reducing apoptosis, and restoring barrier integrity. Intravitreal administration of B022 in DR mice mitigated retinal vascular leakage, reduced apoptosis, and rebalanced M1/M2 polarization.

Our study identifies NIK as a master regulator of microglial polarization in DR via non-canonical NF-κB signaling. By disrupting BRB integrity, NIK-driven neuroinflammation is a critical pathogenic mechanism. The NIK inhibitor B022 demonstrates strong therapeutic potential, positioning NIK as a novel molecular target for treating diabetic retinopathy.
